Events & IPC contracts

Versioned bounded input, normalized event envelopes, exact fingerprints, and host output.

Current invited beta scope

This guide retains earlier milestone design and evidence. The current ten-tester beta preparation uses ad-hoc signatures and is not notarized. Production Cloud API deployment is verified; the signed native client connects through authenticated service IPC; genuine hosted inference remains pending. Claude Code 2.1.290 callback allow/deny, timeout, outage and exact-action native human review checks pass using a local model double; Codex coverage remains unverified. Earlier pending statements describe their original milestone. No public download is published.

Normalized event v1

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "event_id": "sample-event-id",
  "agent": "claude_code",
  "source_session_id": "sample-session-id",
  "agent_sub_id": null,
  "source_turn_id": null,
  "source_tool_call_id": "sample-tool-call-id",
  "kind": "pre_tool_use",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-08T12:00:00Z",
  "cwd": "/Users/dev/projects/widget",
  "repo_root": "/Users/dev/projects/widget",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "action_type": "shell_exec",
  "args_summary": "Proposed outbound transfer referencing a credential",
  "risk_features": ["sensitive_file_reference", "outbound_upload"],
  "redaction_count": 2,
  "raw_input_truncated": false,
  "action_fingerprint": "sha256-of-canonical-original-action",
  "metadata": {"host_permission_mode": "default"}
}

This is a sanitized illustrative envelope, not an accepted live request. Supported event kinds are session_start, user_prompt, pre_tool_use, post_tool_use, post_tool_failure, session_end, and instruction_loaded. Action types include shell_exec, file_read, file_write, file_edit, network, mcp, subagent, and other.

Live IPC v2 contracts

MVP2.0 introduced the additive v2 codec and DTOs. Subsequent local work implements the private Unix listener, kernel peer credentials, running-code authentication and bounded transport cancellation. The socket directory is 0700 and the socket is 0600. Actual altered-family peers fail. The ordinary hook executable remains disabled until host acceptance passes.

A frame is a four-byte network-order length followed by exactly one JSON payload. Bounds are 1 MiB per request, 16 KiB per reply, depth 32, 64 KiB of encoded string content, 1,024 members per object and 2,048 elements per array. Duplicate decoded keys, unexpected typed fields, invalid UTF-8, unknown versions and unsupported precision are rejected.

The v2 request carries protocol_version, request_id, request_kind, adapter, adapter_version, received_at_ms, hard_deadline_ms, host_version, invocation_nonce and host_payload. Original host input stays transient and must not be copied into logs, SQLite or remote requests.

Replies bind request_id and contain only no_override or deny, with bounded evidence and decision metadata. Execution remains unknown. No override preserves host permissions; it grants no execution authority. Codec deadline checks around Foundation are cooperative rather than preemptive. Legacy v1 readers remain unchanged.

Exact action binding

Canonical SHA-256 input contains provider, session, optional turn, tool-call ID, tool name, working directory, and original tool input. MVP2 requires a fresh 128-bit system-random invocation nonce even when the host provides a call ID. Include subagent identity in the approval’s exact scope and isolate simultaneous sessions.

The digest uses original input, not a model-generated title or redacted command summary. Foundation numeric parsing rejects values outside supported exact decimal bounds rather than allowing distinct originals to round to the same action representation.

A fingerprint binds the observed invocation. It does not grant cryptographic control over later nested processes or transport continuations.

Authenticated UI mutations

The native control plane now uses authenticated NSXPCConnection. Approval mutations validate peer audit tokens and code identity and remain absent from the CLI event socket. Exact bindings, pending state, monotonic expiry and durable compare-and-swap transitions are tested. Restart and clear abort unconsumed authority.

The separate developer-only local API control carries allowlisted operations and fixed samples. UI replies omit bearer tokens. Mutation request IDs resist replay; results have no live history or protection authority. Real hosts waiting on native approval and notification actions still require operational acceptance.

Provider verdict contract

AnalysisProvider offers availability and deadline-bound analysis with explicit modes: anthropicBYOK, traceRookCloudDemo, and localRulesOnly. A model verdict contains schema version, category, severity, confidence, suspicious flag, rationale, evidence, recommended action, drift, and limitations.

Production decoding enumerates values, caps lengths, rejects additional properties, validates confidence, and refuses execution instructions. The demo provider only accepts demo-origin requests; it cannot truthfully analyze a real session.

Provisional Cloud API

CloudAPIClient has a fixture implementation in MVP1. Future account, device-registration, usage, plans, analysis, and incident routes are provisional versioned contracts. They are not endpoints implemented by this static site or by a real TraceRook Cloud service.

No auth, login, enrollment, billing, or subscription behavior is implied by a sample account screen.

Based on the MVP1 specification, the additive MVP2 specification, and the acceptance matrix · October 8, 2026.
